segments.name: Light adjustable lenses
segments.description: Sells light adjustable intraocular lenses and light delivery devices to cataract surgeons, who customize patients' vision after surgery.
segments.evidence: The Company determined that it operates and manages its business (including its non-U.S. subsidiaries) in one reportable segment: the research and development, manufacture and sale of light adjustable lenses and related capital equipment.

revenueModel.text: Ophthalmology practices and surgeons buy the light delivery device and lenses; patients pay out-of-pocket fees for premium procedures beyond insurer-covered cataract surgery.
revenueModel.evidence: In the U.S., Medicare and private insurers typically cover the full cost of spherical monofocal IOL procedures, while premium IOL procedures require patients to pay an incremental out-of-pocket fee, typically ranging from $2,000 to $5,000 per eye depending on the specific premium IOL used.
